{{recipesummary|category=Sauce recipes|yield=2 cups|time=½ hour|difficulty=3}}
{{recipe}} | [[Cookbook:Cuisine of the United States|American cuisine]] | [[Cookbook:Cuisine of Italy|Italian cuisine]] | [[Cookbook:Vegetarian cuisine|Vegetarian Cuisine]]

==Ingredients==
* 4 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tablespoons]] [[Cookbook:Olive Oil|olive]] or [[Cookbook:Vegetable Oil|vegetable oil]]
* 4 large yellow or white [[Cookbook:Onion|onions]], [[Cookbook:Slicing|sliced]] into thin strips
* ½ [[Cookbook:Cup|cups]] white granulated [[Cookbook:Sugar|sugar]]
* ¼ cup [[Cookbook:Vinegar|balsamic vinegar]]
* ¼ [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|teaspoon]] [[Cookbook:Salt|salt]]
* ⅛ teaspoon coarse ground [[Cookbook:Pepper|black pepper]]

==Procedure==
# Heat oil in a large [[Cookbook:Frying Pan|frying pan]] over medium heat. Add onions, and [[Cookbook:Sauté|sauté]], stirring, for about 15 minutes, or until they begin to brown. Do not cook over high heat, as the outside of the onions will char too quickly before the insides have softened and sweetened.
# When onions have softened and turned a light golden brown, add sugar. Continue stirring until sugar melts and begins to bubble.
# As the onions turn a richer brown, clear a space in the center of the pan. Pour balsamic vinegar directly onto the hot pan, then stir it into onions.
# When vinegar has reduced, leaving a syrupy coating on the onions, turn off the heat.
# Stir in salt and pepper, and allow onions to cool.

==Uses==

* Used in [[Cookbook:Focaccia|Focaccia]] ([[Cookbook:Focaccia with Onion Marmalade, Blue Cheese, and Walnuts|Focaccia with Onion Marmalade, Blue Cheese, and Walnuts]])
